Remarks

This type contains two categories of helpers:

  • Gameplay / arcade helpers such as frame-rate-independent drag scaling and simplified motion utilities that are convenient in a game engine but are not strict real-world physics.
  • Physics-inspired helpers whose formulas are closer to classical mechanics, such as inverse-square attraction or quadratic drag. These still operate in engine units, not necessarily SI units.

In this engine, a returned vector is usually meant to be passed to AddForce(Vector2), unless the method remarks explicitly say otherwise. AddForce(Vector2) converts a force-like vector into acceleration by dividing by mass. A mass less than or equal to zero is treated as 1 by the helpers in this class.

Be aware that some older APIs use the word Force for gameplay damping values that are actually applied as a change in velocity rather than a Newtonian force. In particular, CalculateDragForce(Vector2, float, float) and its directional overload return the velocity delta produced by drag over a time step, while CalculateDragForceRealistic(Vector2, float, float, float) returns a force-like vector based on the drag equation.

Methods named Calculate* return values and do not mutate inputs, except where a compatibility overload is explicitly documented otherwise. Methods named Apply* mutate one or more PhysicsObject instances by adding forces or changing velocity.

ApplyFrictionForce(PhysicsObject, Vector2, float)

Applies a gameplay-style friction force to the specified obj based on its velocity and the given surface normal. The friction force acts opposite to the tangent component of motion and is scaled by the provided frictionForce. The force is only applied if the object is moving and the tangent component of the velocity is non-zero.

Returns

bool

Returns true if a friction force was applied; otherwise, false.

Calculates the drag-induced velocity delta to apply to an object over the given time step. This is a gameplay damping helper, not a Newtonian force calculation.

Parameters

velocity Vector2

The time step over which to apply the drag.

Calculates a force that gets stronger with distance and direction. The force scales with distance squared and the mass of the attraction object! Calculates a reverse-attraction force between two objects that scales with distance squared. This is a physics-inspired gameplay helper, not a real-world gravity formula.

Remarks

The returned vectors are force-like engine-space values intended for AddForce(Vector2). Masses less than or equal to zero are treated as 1.
